chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Detroit pianists who sounded like Art Tatum
summary: Collins names Willie Hawkins of Detroit and Lanny Scott of Cleveland as pianists who sounded like Tatum, and mentions Al McKibbon and Kelly Martin.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It was Capitol, yeah, yeah. I also want to go back to Detroit, we were talking about Gerald Wilson (up there) when we picked him didn't we. And at this time I met a pianist who played so much like Art Tatum, his name was Willie Hawkins. And he finally came out here but he got ill and he went back to Detroit, and I think he died. And this is where I met Al McKibbon, during that same time, and we got Gerald Wilson out of there.
Al McKibbons from Detroit, and I met another very fine drummer at that time, Kelly Martin. He was a drummer with Errol in later years. Very fine drummer. But

I want to say Willie Hawkins, these are the two guys that really sounded to me like Art, was Willie Hawkins and it was another guy in Cleveland, from Cleveland rather. Lanny Scott. Did I mention Lanny, that I saw him playing with Jonah's band in Boston this past season, with Cozy Cole and John Brown playing bass. But I just heard that Lanny just died also. But he was one of the few guys that really sounded like Art. You know, well he's from Cleveland too, and Art was just his idol.
